q: A catalyst does not affect the equilibrium concentrations, and there is no change in equilibrium. (2024)
e: A catalyst increases the rates of forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium concentrations remain unchanged.

q: The reaction is completely stopped at equilibrium. (2024)
e: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic, meaning forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates rather than stopping.

q: The formation of products is favoured by high temperature in an exothermic reaction. (2024)
e: In an exothermic reaction, lowering the temperature favours product formation, whereas higher temperature favours reactants.

q: If a reversible reaction is in a closed system, the system can reach a state called equilibrium. (2024)
e: In a closed system where matter cannot enter or escape, reversible reactions are able to attain chemical equilibrium.

q: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and products of chemical equilibrium are present in a single phase. (2024)
e: In heterogeneous equilibrium, reactants and products exist in more than one physical phase.

q: At equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal. (2024)
e: Equilibrium is defined by the point at which the forward reaction rate equals the reverse reaction rate.

q: The formation of product is favoured by high temperature in an endothermic reaction. (2025)
e: Endothermic reactions absorb heat, so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium toward product formation.

q: Matter can neither be gained nor lost in a closed system. (2025)
e: A closed system prevents mass transfer across its boundary, keeping total mass constant.

q: Industrial processes are usually designed to give the minimum possible yield of products. (2025)
e: Industrial chemical processes are optimized to achieve the maximum yield of desired products as efficiently as possible.

q: The sublimation of iodine crystals is the solid-vapour heterogeneous equilibrium state. (2025)
e: Iodine sublimation involves solid and gas phases coexisting at equilibrium, making it a heterogeneous state.

q: If the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides of the reversible chemical equation. (2025)
e: When the total moles of gaseous reactants and products are equal, pressure changes do not shift the equilibrium position.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate. (2025)
e: Dynamic equilibrium means both forward and backward processes proceed continuously at equal speeds.

q: The effect of changing the pressure on a reaction involving gases is negligible. (2025)
e: Pressure changes significantly impact gaseous equilibria unless total moles of gas remain equal on both sides.

q: The units of equilibrium constant depend on the form of the equilibrium expression. (2025)
e: The units of Kc or Kp are determined by the stoichiometric coefficients in the specific equilibrium expression.

q: A dynamic equilibrium exists once a reversible reaction occurs. (2026)
e: Reversible reactions in closed systems establish dynamic equilibrium once forward and reverse reaction rates balance.

q: A chemical equilibrium is said to be a dynamic nature. (2026)
e: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic because molecular transformations continue in both directions constantly.

q: The units of equilibrium constant depend on the form of the equilibrium expression. (2026)
e: The overall unit depends on the stoichiometric powers of reactants and products in the balanced reaction.

q: Both K_p and K_c cannot be applied for the gaseous reactions. (2026)
e: Both Kp (using partial pressures) and Kc (using molar concentrations) can be applied to reactions involving gases.

q: Reversible reactions that happen in a closed system eventually reach equilibrium. (2026)
e: Given sufficient time in a closed environment, reversible chemical reactions arrive at equilibrium.

q: The decomposition of N2O4 (colourless) to NO2 (reddish-brown) is exothermic reaction. (2026)
e: The decomposition of N2O4 into NO2 absorbs heat, making it an endothermic process.

q: Decreasing the temperature would favour the exothermic reaction. (2026)
e: Lowering the temperature shifts equilibrium in the direction that releases heat (exothermic direction).
